question: Does the evidence show that the Autel EVO Max 4N returns home after losing its link?
stop_reason: claims still failing after the revision limit

intake.focus: Autel EVO Max 4N lost link behavior
intake.reason: Question asks if evidence shows automatic return to home after loss of control link; sources include manuals and incident reports for Autel EVO Max 4N in the collection.

brief.short_answer: FAA guidance indicates reestablishing the control link after a lost-link hazard and discontinuing flight or avoiding further operations until testing the control link. The Autel EVO Max 4N manual states RTH is triggered when Return to Home is active or Auto RTH is selected. It also says the drone will continue flying until the disconnection message appears, and that a link restoration within 10 seconds will automatically return control to the remote. Incident reports (unverified) claim the UAS lost control shortly after takeoff and that Return To Home failed. Gaps and conflicts: it is unclear whether RTH was engaged in the incident, whether the 10-second auto-return applied, and how model-specific Autel behavior reconciles with FAA guidance.
